l1_words.meaning: a set book or text to read for a course

pattern_explanation: These Polish words and their English counterparts come from the same Latin or French sources, so their forms stayed close, but over time their meanings drifted apart.
false_friend_warning: Each Polish word looks almost identical to an English word but means something different: the Polish word for 'possibly' resembles 'eventually', which means 'in the end'; the Polish word for 'nice' resembles 'sympathetic'; the Polish word for 'current' resembles 'actual', which means 'real'; and the Polish word for a set reading resembles 'lecture', which means a talk. Learners who translate these literally will choose the wrong English word.
